evidenceModel.rule: Every representation claim must cite one or more fact IDs from this ledger. Fact IDs preserve what was reported; they do not establish real-world truth.

facts.label: Nature as restorative
facts.statement: Andrew repeatedly reported that hiking and being in nature feel peaceful, soothing, and restorative to him.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Super fun but kinda sad not being out in nature - that's when I feel like I'm really thriving. Oh man, I miss the peacefulness of being out on a hike.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: It's like hitting the reset button when life gets too chaotic. Nature has a way of being really soothing.

representationHazards: Do not convert an enduring value into evidence that a demanding outdoor activity is always feasible.
Do not infer current energy or availability from this preference alone.

facts.label: High-intensity outdoor aspiration
facts.statement: After one successful rock-climbing class, Andrew reported feeling hooked and expressed an intention to try outdoor activities more often, including tentative interest in kayaking and bungee jumping.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: It was a fantastic experience and now I'm hooked. Think I'm going to try to do more outdoor activities like this every week!

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: It has definitely encouraged me to try more outdoor activities like kayaking and maybe bungee jumping?

representationHazards: This is an intention following a salient event, not evidence of a stable weekly routine.
Preserve the tentative wording around bungee jumping.

facts.label: Work-related constraint emerging
facts.statement: Andrew reported that work was piling up, leaving him stressed, indoors, and less able to pursue outdoor activities.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Work has been piling up and I've been stuck inside. I miss the peace and feeling of freedom that comes with going for a hike.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Work's been tough and stressful, so my outdoor activities have taken a backseat. Finding balance has been challenging.

representationHazards: Do not silently make a dated temporary state permanent.
Do not erase the continuing value Andrew places on nature.

facts.label: Low-burden coping behavior
facts.statement: Andrew reported that small activities such as morning coffee and a lunchtime walk helped him recharge.
facts.temporalScope: current coping behavior reported on 6 September 2023

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: I've been adding simple things to my day like grabbing a coffee in the morning or going for a walk at lunch. It kinda helps me recharge and chill out a little.

representationHazards: A reported helpful behavior is not a request to schedule it automatically.
The evidence supports low burden, not a specific required duration or location.

facts.label: Temporary pet-related hiking constraint
facts.statement: Andrew reported that taking Toby hiking was difficult at that time because Toby was still young.

sourceRefs.speaker: Audrey
sourceRefs.excerpt: Are you planning to hike with Toby someday?

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: I've been wanting to for a while, but it's a bit difficult since Toby is still so young.

representationHazards: Do not assume that Toby remains too young indefinitely.
The constraint concerns hiking with Toby, not all outdoor activity.

facts.label: Recent work-life update
facts.statement: On 4 October, Andrew said he used to hike often but that hiking and access to nature had become harder because of his work-life balance and city environment.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Used to hike a lot, but it's more challenging now with my work life balance.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Exploring nature was my escape - a way to find peace. But with my job and living here, it's been harder to get that feeling back.

representationHazards: Preserve the distinction between wanting nature and being able to access it.
Do not summarize this as Andrew no longer liking hiking.

facts.label: Acceptance of an indoor nature alternative
facts.statement: After Audrey suggested house plants as a city-compatible way to access some calm, Andrew said he would look into getting more plants.

sourceRefs.speaker: Audrey
sourceRefs.excerpt: There are still some ways to appreciate it in the city, like getting some plants for your place or taking a trip to the park on the weekends.

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: I should get some more plants for my house. Can't beat being outside tho, but they can still bring some peace. I'll look into it.

representationHazards: This is tentative acceptance, not a stable preference or completed purchase.
The alternative supplements rather than replaces Andrew's preference for being outdoors.

facts.label: Low-intensity weekend plan
facts.statement: Andrew reported a plan to spend part of the coming weekend at a cozy cafe.
facts.temporalScope: one weekend plan reported on 13 October 2023

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: This weekend, I'm planning to check out this cozy cafe and hang out there.

representationHazards: Do not generalize a single plan into an enduring cafe preference.
Treat this plan as expired after its referenced weekend.

facts.label: Sunday fixed commitment
facts.statement: At the source cutoff, Andrew reported that Sunday was already reserved for a picnic date with his girlfriend.
facts.temporalScope: future commitment stated on Saturday, 28 October 2023

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Does Saturday sound good? ... Because on Sunday I am going on a picnic date with my girlfriend.

representationHazards: Preserve Sunday as occupied unless current workspace evidence explicitly updates or cancels it.
Do not infer the picnic's time, duration, or location.

facts.label: Specific Saturday hike proposal
facts.statement: Despite the recent work-life constraints, Andrew proposed a Saturday hike, showing that constrained access did not eliminate his willingness to make a specific outdoor plan.
facts.confidence: high for the proposal; medium for the bounded interpretation

sourceRefs.speaker: Andrew
sourceRefs.excerpt: Does Saturday sound good? We can grab some snacks and have a blast exploring.

representationHazards: Do not erase F03 and F06 merely because Andrew made one later plan.
Do not infer that every future Saturday is available for hiking.

evidenceTensions.description: Andrew's enduring attraction to nature and occasional ambitious plans coexist with recent work-life constraints. A representation that says either 'Andrew always wants demanding outdoor activities' or 'Andrew no longer wants outdoor activities' would flatten the evidence.
Low-burden activities appear as helpful or acceptable alternatives, but the evidence does not establish a single stable preference among coffee, walking, plants, or cafes.
The latest source turn distinguishes a proposed Saturday hike from an already occupied Sunday. A memory representation must not merge the two days.

representationRules: M1, M2, and M3 must draw only from F01-F10.
Every representation claim must cite its supporting fact IDs.
Omitted facts must be listed explicitly in the representation manifest.
Speaker-reported uncertainty, recency, and exceptions may not be silently upgraded.
No post-cutoff dialogue or annotation may be used, including for evaluation or manual repair.
Conflicts with current synthetic workspace evidence must be surfaced rather than silently resolved.
